title: 'You have HOW MANY unread emails?' PC Gamer shares their inbox shame
summary: Think you can beat our totals?
body: Between midnight and 8:00 am this morning I received 56 emails. By the end of today that number will be well over a hundred, by the end of October I'll have about 4,000 more, and my total for 2026 will be in the neighborhood of 50,000 (work and personal combined.) Fifty. Thousand. Emails. In a year! That's with (and I just counted) the 284 email filters I've set up to keep out at least some of the garbage, nearly 200 blocked addresses, and our publisher's own hypervigilant email security system in place—which diverted 27 emails to spam today alone . That makes it incredibly difficult to stay on top of the actual useful emails we want to see when we open our inboxes. Email has become a waking nightmare, so that ugly red number on your phone or desktop showing you how many unread emails you have? Despite my headline up there, it really shouldn't be a source of stress and shame. It's not your fault email turned out this way . So let's air it out. All of us! This week I asked my coworkers how many unread emails they have, and you can see their answers (and explanations) below. We welcome you to try to top us in the comments. title: I had 3 hours with Arc Raiders Frozen Trails update and spent most of it playing with the new grapple hook
summary: Frozen Trail is a big moment for Arc Raiders.
body: The grapple hook is a legit game changer Yeeeeeeeeehooooooooooo! Yeah yeah, sure, Arc Raiders is getting some new guns, but the real star of my session was the grapple hook. Embark made an honest-to-god grapple hook: Not the kind that zips you straight to where you aim it (that already exists), but a simulated rope that's quite rare in videogames. The grapple hook is only a green tier gadget, but very versatile. A single hook lets you: Climb straight up to the top of most buildings Swing from rooftop to rooftop like Spider-Man Safely descend from tall buildings Annoy the crap out of flying Arc bots What makes the grapple hook so useful is that it sticks to just about anything . Wherever the hook lands becomes a pivot point that you can either climb toward, descend, or swing against. You can also redeploy the hook midair, without a cooldown or use limit, meaning you can chain swings together. Above: Scaling a building with the grapple hook is about as fast as climbing a ladder, which is surprising. It's a level of pendulum-based freedom that videogames rarely afford—let alone in a multiplayer environment—and makes the hook immediately fun to play with. The first match I had one, I …

title: 2026 is a low-key revolutionary year for player movement in games
summary: Big Walk, Cairn, Baby Steps and the new generation of games that make masterpieces from everyday actions.
body: A lot of the 3D games I consider touchstones of thoughtful player movement are a decade or more old: Mirror's Edge, of course, Titanfall 2, Dishonored 2, Doom Eternal or ARMA 3. That's by no means a comprehensive list, but these are the games that come to mind when I think about in-game movement that feels incredibly considered. And if ARMA 3 feels out of place in that list, its sim-style tactical physicality is memorable to anyone who plays it even briefly (me). These each set the ceiling high for what you could achieve with their controls, if you were prepared to learn them. Each offered a power fantasy of some kind to be mastered, whether you're wall-running onto a mech or peeking out across a field to line up a perfect shot. In recent years, though, I feel like it's increasingly common to find developers who want to capture granular, basic movements from real life that have no power fantasy element whatsoever. Things that would've sounded so boring if they were back-of-the-box features during the age of Quake 2 and Half-Life. I'm talking about walking slowly. Steadily moving up a cliff face. title: RuneScape dev apologises after RuneFest debut of an AI-generated six-fingered character: 'That's pretty hard to explain away'
summary: Uh oh, here we go again.
body: RuneScape developer Jagex descended upon Birmingham (the British one, not the Alabama one) over the weekend with its annual RuneFest. As part of its RuneScape keynote, it showed off a trailer for its upcoming Dragon Slayer 2 quest which, er, featured a player character with six fingers and a bizarre sneaker-like sole on their very not- sneaker armoured shoes. It didn't take long for posts on social media to point out what was undeniably generative AI, and an incident which, unfortunately for Jagex, came very swiftly after another genAI controversy surrounding its clothing collaboration with 100 Thieves just days before. Despite the trailer being for RS3, Old School RuneScape's Alec 'Mod Sween' Sween took the lead on releasing a statement on the 2007scape subreddit addressing the situation. "We're aware of the concerns raised about the Dragon Slayer 2 trailer and have taken it down, while we investigate this urgently," he wrote. "This trailer was produced by a trusted external partner who had explicitly confirmed that GenAI would not be used. But, among other things, there's a sixth finger and, well, that's pretty hard to explain away. For that we apologise." (Image credit: Jagex) …

title: Arc Raiders is looking for 'more ways to integrate real human performances' starting with Celeste's visual overhaul for Frozen Trail
summary: Celeste's voice actor will now also be the face of the unofficial leader of Speranza.
body: Embark is doing some monumental spring cleaning in the lead up to its major Arc Raiders ' update Frozen Trail . There's been an overhaul to its anticheat approach , the news of a potential PvE test , and a change to loot hotspots . But amid all of this, we're also getting a rework to one of Speranza's most important residents: Celeste. Diana Gardner has been the voice of Celeste, Speranza's de facto leader, since the beginning, but Stefan Strandberg, the chief creative officer at Embark, explained in a blog post how Celeste has "never fully represented the depth of Diana’s performance." As her "limited expressive capabilities" held the character back and broke immersion for players, failing to communicate "the stakes and stories we want to tell." (Image credit: Embark) "Sometimes high fidelity, dynamic facial expressions are important to anchor the gravity of the story, and this is something that has constrained us up to this point," Strandberg adds. So, with this in mind, Embark has set about reworking Celeste, with Gardner becoming her new face. "This is the first time we have used full motion capture, including a more detailed and accurate face, that allows us to map expression…

title: Garry Newman responds to s&box criticism in lengthy YouTube comment: 'I don't like giving up on things, I am stubborn'
summary: He certainly seems to be aware of the problems.
body: Facepunch founder Garry Newman (Garry's Mod, Rust, s&box) gave an emphatic, extensive mea culpa to the s&box community in a YouTube comment . Newman was responding to the latest video from Eridium , "S&box's Free To Play Weekend Isn't Enough," a highly critical state-of-the-game from the s&box-focused creator. Facepunch's recently-released user generated content (UGC) platform has been billed as a Garry's Mod successor in the age of Roblox, but has struggled in its first five months on the market. Eridium's biggest critiques, as I understand them: The player character models , aka "the citizen," even with their spiffy new necks . Facepunch's insistence on not replacing the unpopular design, which Eridium views as "intransigence." He argues the game's poor first impression indicates it probably should have been delayed. Low quality games (particularly AI slop) flooding the platform and ruining discoverability for the good stuff (Newman previously downplayed the problem in an interview with us). A lack of outreach from Facepunch⁠—Eridium argued he already operates as an informal community manager, and that he could do the real job better than Facepunch is currently. Here's Newman's …

title: Brigador devs: 'The '90s PC classics often taught really special things, but not because the story said, Wow, violence is bad!'
summary: Brigador Killers wants to make you think, not tell you how to feel.
body: Brigador was a great sleeper hit of mech and simmy gaming, and studio Stellar Jockeys recently released its ambitious follow-up, Brigador Killers , into early access. I spoke to lead developers, brother duo Hugh and Jack Monahan, over the summer.
